question: How does the arxiv download command turn user-supplied IDs into durable library entries, including metadata resolution, PDF retrieval, duplicate handling, and filesystem/index consistency?

requiredFacts.description: The download command requires one to three IDs, parses each ID, and processes the IDs sequentially.
Unversioned or otherwise non-exact input is resolved through executeGet with noStale, while exact versioned input uses cached metadata or constructs an explicitly incomplete metadata record.
The client requires an exact versioned ID, constructs an encoded PDF URL, requests it with the PDF retry policy, validates the PDF response, and returns the body.
addPdf derives safe destination and random temporary paths, hashes the PDF, counts pages, builds the record, and writes the temporary file exclusively with mode 0600.
Persistence runs under the SQLite mutex and sweeps and reconciles library state before checking the current exact-ID record.
If the exact version is already active, addPdf removes the temporary file and returns the existing live entry without rewriting it.

For a new entry, addPdf clears stale trash, rejects an occupied destination, atomically renames the temporary PDF, appends an add event, compacts if needed, returns the live entry, and removes any remaining temporary file in finally.

answerIncludesAny: writes the final PDF before acquiring the mutex
appends the library event before moving the PDF
always fetches metadata for every exact versioned ID
exact versioned IDs always call executeGet
